$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-08-31 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report b3d95aa2. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v22 index for sub2api (INDEX cb30eed1) built by publish-tee-images run 33363884536 from commit 306b1bc77; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor was not touched, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release ships two changes. First, a newly connected OAuth supply account is now probed synchronously at attach time, so it can start serving within seconds instead of the 20-30 minutes it previously spent waiting on two background polls - a wait that observed nothing, being merely the product of a 5-minute sweep interval and a 15-minute gap between the two probes required for promotion. The relay onboarding path already probed at submit time for exactly this reason; the OAuth path did not, on the grounds that the token exchange proves the credential works - but that only proves a token can be minted, not that the subscription can still serve inference. The attach probe deliberately gets no special case: it participates in the existing state machine as the first probe and is judged by the SAME eligibility rule as the background sweep, so how long a new account waits is a matter of probation configuration rather than of which onboarding path it took. Probe failure does not roll back onboarding - the account is created, owned and pooled, and a failed probe leaves it in review with a visible reason. Second, suspicious-usage findings from the abuse detector are now written to the existing ops_alert_events table. Previously the detector's entire output was a single log line, and this deployment runs with public_logs disabled - the correct setting for confidential compute - so nothing could read it: 'detect but do not act' amounted to doing nothing at all. Deduplication is per user rather than per rule, because these events share rule_id 0 and the existing rule-keyed scheme would have let the first flagged user suppress everyone else's alerts silently. Automatic throttling remains off; the signal comes first. Earlier in this line: proof-v21 (supplier self-service re-authorization), v20 (supply concurrency 3->15), v19 (abuse detection, shipped disabled), v18 (take-offline copy), v17 (reference-source fix + first-screen 1332KB->118KB), v16/v15 (two-sided marketplace). osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation. Deploy note: this rollout completed in 89 seconds with no incident, unlike proof-v21, which hit a Phala prod5 outage and boot-looped for about forty minutes when dstack-prepare.sh could not reach the gateway to register the CVM.
